source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Rely on the electronic security device after activation because required parent-infant identification verification then becomes redundant.","B":"Perform identification verification only when a staff member suspects a security problem rather than as required by the established plan.","C":"Follow all applicable components of the newborn security plan, including required identification verification; one electronic control does not replace staff checks.","D":"Suspend routine newborn security procedures when the unit has had no recent incidents because security plans apply only after a documented threat."}}
source_row.rationale: The current NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly includes following security plans and procedures, including newborn security, within Safety and Infection Prevention and Control. Layered facility procedures must be followed rather than substituting one control for the plan.
source_row.source_detail: Overview of Content — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: “Follow security plan and procedures (e.g., newborn security...)”. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A maternity unit uses a newborn security plan that includes parent-infant identification checks and other safeguards. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
